subject: design-technology
title: Gears & Pulleys
welcome_lead: Teeth, ratios and how machines change motion.
meta_desc: KS3 D&T: gear ratios, types of gears, pulley systems.

concepts.def: Toothed wheel that meshes with another.
Driven teeth divided by driver teeth.
Wheel with rope or belt around it.
Gear between two others — keeps direction.
How much a machine multiplies force.

walkthroughs.body_html: When two gears mesh, they spin in opposite directions. If the driver has 10 teeth and the driven has 20, the gear ratio is 2:1 — driven turns half as fast but with twice the force.
Pulleys use a rope or belt. A single pulley just changes direction. A two-pulley system halves the effort needed but doubles the rope length pulled.
A bevel gear turns motion through 90 degrees — used in hand drills. An idler gear sits between two gears so they spin the same direction.
